target: the field's low-maturity evaluation record as a ceiling on IVR's value
note: (P/anticipatory-application) Radianti's own reading is that the evaluation gaps (theory-thin, usability-over-outcomes) are a fixable research-agenda item, not a verdict against immersion's promise -- an implicit contestation of the more skeptical value-added reading Mayer et al. (ped-sec-07) draw from overlapping evidence.

target: more immersion -> more learning <-> immersion adds presence but not learning
note: (P/anticipatory-application) Radianti et al. occupy the affordance-optimism pole of debate axis 1 (cluster plan §4): the field's own evaluation weaknesses are read as evidence of *underexploited* potential (18 application domains, rising publication counts, still 'experimental') rather than as evidence that immersion fails to translate into learning -- a stance that concedes Mayer et al.'s (ped-sec-07) diagnosis of weak evaluation while rejecting the ceiling Mayer draws from it. Precise stance: affordance-optimism tempered by methodological critique, not naive boosterism -- Radianti documents the identical evaluation-quality gaps Mayer highlights but treats them as a maturity/agenda problem, not a verdict.

target: media-comparison designs are informative <-> methods-not-media / value-added is the valid paradigm
note: (P/anticipatory-application) Radianti's own inclusion criterion sorts studies by technology type (immersive HMD vs. excluded desktop VR/CAVE), implicitly treating the medium itself as the primary variable worth reviewing -- the opposite emphasis from Mayer et al.'s (ped-sec-07) argument that methods/value-added design, not medium, should guide both research and practice. Not a claim Radianti makes about Mayer; this cluster's own placement of the two reviews on opposite sides of the axis.

target: immersion as objective technological attribute (Slater & Wilbur) <-> immersion as subjective psychological state (Witmer & Singer)
note: Radianti adopts the technological view operationally, for inclusion-criteria tractability only, explicitly declining to resolve the underlying theoretical dispute between the two camps (FE, p.2-3).

(P/anticipatory-application) Radianti's central diagnosis -- immersive VR is 'mostly experimental and development work rather than being applied regularly in actual teaching' -- makes the VLE King-Salvo entry's status as an actually deployed, routine-use learning environment an exception this review's own base-rate finding would predict is rare; useful for framing the VLE's deployment status as noteworthy rather than typical.
